**Proposed mechanism:** ASPNAT (HGNC:24428) —DISRUPTS→ glutamate-aspartate transport (REACT:R-HSA-109580); glutamate-aspartate transport (REACT:R-HSA-109580) —LEADS_TO→ seizure (HP:0001250); SLC25A12 (HGNC:10975) —DISRUPTS→ mitochondrial calcium uptake (GO:0006827); mitochondrial calcium uptake (GO:0006827) —LEADS_TO→ developmental delay (HP:0001263). Loss-of-function mutations in ASPNAT disrupt glutamate-aspartate transport, leading to phenotypes such as seizures. Concurrently, loss-of-function mutations in SLC25A12 impair mitochondrial calcium uptake, contributing to phenotypes like developmental delay. The convergence occurs on the broader cellular processes affected by these disruptions, impacting neuronal excitability and development.

**How to falsify it:** If pathogenic variants in ASPNAT are found to be exclusively associated with phenotypes unrelated to neurological dysfunction, or if pathogenic variants in SLC25A12 do not impact mitochondrial calcium homeostasis, this hypothesis would be falsified. Additionally, the absence of shared neurological phenotypes between patients with ASPNAT and SLC25A12 mutations would weaken the hypothesis. _(variant: A common pathogenic variant (allele frequency > 1% in gnomAD) in either ASPNAT or SLC25A12 would challenge the hypothesis of these genes causing rare diseases.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared mechanistic basis involving glutamate-aspartate transport and mitochondrial calcium regulation could lead to the identification of common therapeutic targets for both ASPNAT-related diseases and developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 39, potentially involving modulators of these pathways.
